longRunningTraceSamplingRate.description: Sampling rate for traces force-emitted because they exceeded the configured maxSessionLength. Routed through a dedicated 'long_running' percentile bucket — distinct from the structural 'incomplete' bucket — so operators can monitor and tune separately.

maxSessionLength.description: Upper bound on how long a single trace assembly session may accumulate spans in memory before being force-emitted. Protects against long-running traces that would otherwise hold spans in the assembly buffer indefinitely. When the cap is hit, the trace is classified as long-running and later spans form a new session. Must be strictly greater than maxTraceDelay.

maxTraceDelay.description: The maximum time to wait for all spans of a trace to arrive before assembling the trace. This determines the size of the tumbling window used for trace assembly. Traces that span longer than this duration may be assembled as partial traces. Should be set based on the expected maximum trace duration in your system. Large values may lead to memory issues if traces are too long and will delay sending traces to the sink by that amount. The pipeline may also fail if configured too high.

quantileSamplingTiers.description: List of quantile sampling tiers for performance-based sampling. Each tier defines a percentile threshold, sampling rate, and label. Traces ABOVE each quantile get the corresponding sampling rate and are labeled with the tier's label. Evaluated in descending quantile order. A tier at quantile 0.0 is a catch-all that matches unconditionally, giving the fastest traces a baseline rate; without one, traces below the lowest configured quantile are dropped.

put.description: Validates and stores the complete promotion policy on the table. Newly included tag columns, and the columns of exact attribute includes the attribute cap has room for, are added synchronously before the request returns, in the same commit as the policy. Send back the revision the policy was read at to be refused rather than overwrite a change made since; omit it to replace whatever is stored.

requestBody.description: The complete promotion policy document. It is decoded by the same strict codec that reads the stored policy: every field is typed exactly, no unknown field is accepted at any depth, and no value is coerced. It replaces the stored policy rather than patching it, and both groups are required -- a body that omits "tags" or "attributes" is rejected, not read as a request to stop discovery for that group. The cap is the switch: send a group with "cap": 0 to stop it promoting fields it has not seen before, which for attributes includes the paths it includes. That does not blank the group -- the columns the table already carries keep being written. A field is stopped by naming it in that group's exclude list, or, for attributes, by setting "excludeAllByDefault", which stops every path the include list does not cover. Read the current policy and send it back whole, changing only what you mean to change.

400.description: Invalid promotion policy.

409.description: The policy changed since the revision the request was made against; read it again and reapply the change. Or the table kept changing under the request, which a running writer's own evolution can cause; retry.

post.description:
Submit an async job (`streaming` or `batch`). This is an asynchronous operation which returns an identifier (field: `id`) for the job to be created, in the response. The id can be used to query the status of the job using the `GET` jobs endpoint. Job creation lifecycle is represented by the state field in the `GET` response. States represent the following:
 - `PENDING`: Job has been successfully accepted for submission
 - `WAITING`: Job is waiting on other jobs to finish to be submitted.
 - `STARTING`: Job is being transitioned to the `RUNNING` state.
 - `RUNNING`: Job is running.
 - `FAILED` : Job creation failed.

400.description: Bad Request

post.description: Creates a logs or spans backfill batch job from backfill parameters (time window, query, vendor sinks, and optional type-specific fields). The `dataType` selects the built-in logs or spans template. This is an asynchronous batch job: the response returns an identifier (field: `id`) that can be used to query the status of the job using the `GET` jobs endpoint. The server builds the backfill job graph from the parameters, so callers do not assemble it themselves.

400.description: Bad Request

post.description: Submits a job whose results will be returned synchronously as a stream of nd-json. Both streaming and batch jobs using a source with synchronous processing type are supported. The returned data is new-line delimited json log event records. The returned data will be wrapped in an EventRecord object that contains the state of the job. The server will periodically send heartbeats to the client through the same stream so the client knows the server is still alive. The client in return should send a heartbeat back to the server using the `/sync/heartbeat` endpoint to keep the connection alive. The client should use the heartbeat token returned in the EventRecord object to send the heartbeat. The connection will be closed if the client does not send a heartbeat within the timeout period. Additionally, the connection will close if the job fails or finished, or if the job runs for too long. This last timeout is dependent on whether the job is a batch or streaming job.

400.description: Bad Request

post.description: Sends a heartbeat to a synchronous job to keep it alive. This is needed to keep the connection open and to prevent the server from closing it.

400.description: Bad Request

post.summary: Heartbeat a sync job to keep it alive

Updates an asynchronous streaming job. This is an asynchronous operation which returns an identifier (field: id) for the job to be created, in the response. The id can be used to query the status of the job using the GET jobs endpoint. If a change in the job graph is detected, a new version of the job will be created and sent back in the response object. Job update lifecycle is represented by the state field in the GET response. Following states can be expected in the response:
 - PENDING:        Job is in the process of being updated.

 - INFRA_UPDATE:   Job is undergoing an infra change.
